newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European bourse rally fizzles out.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European bourse rally fizzles out.

text.p: This week's record run by European bourses fizzled out on Wednesday after U.S. prices data failed to re-ignite the investor buying spree and Wall Street slipped.
All three of Europe's major stock markets -- London, Paris and Frankfurt -- ended well down following peaks on Tuesday.
The dollar also closed slightly lower in Europe as mark short-covering took its toll on recent star currencies like the Italian lira and British pound.
And the oil market rally that saw world crude prices hit a post-Gulf War high on Tuesday stalled as traders rushed to cash in profits.

By late afternoon in London, December Brent crude oil futures on London's International Petroleum Exchange stood at $23.88 a barrel, 23 cents down on the day and a sharp 52 cents off Wednesday's high.
European markets had been on hold ahead of the U.S. consumer figures for September -- closely watched by bond markets and high-flying stock markets on both sides of the Atlantic.
Economists have become increasingly concerned that rising labour costs in a tightening job market could lead to a pickup in inflation in the months ahead.
In the event, the U.S. Labour Department said consumer prices rose a moderate 0.3 percent, following an increase of 0.1 percent in August.
The numbers steadied European stock markets only briefly and profit-taking took hold again as Wall Street turned lower after a modestly firm start.
By the time Europe closed, the Dow Jones Industrials index was down around 25 points at 5,980 as some technology stocks struggled on earnings that failed to please the market enough.
London stocks, already pressured by downbeat economic news, perked up only for a short while after the U.S. data before resuming their decline.

The FTSE 100 index of leading shares ended down 26.4 points at 4,024.4 after stronger-than-expected unemployment and earnings numbers, together with a strong rise in public borrowing combined to weigh on the market.
The British data brought home the realisation that interest rates would have to go up, said Andy Hartwill, strategist at SocGen in London.
"This market is being driven by the perpetual hope that interest rate increases are something you read about in fairy stories."
French shares fell as Wall Street turned down, consolidating after reaching a year high on Tuesday.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended down 9.76 points, or 0.45 percent, at 2,158.52. The CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,157 from 2,172 on Tuesday's close.
"The decline today was on profit-taking. But that could turn into a downward correction in the coming days," a dealer said.
German shares closed bourse dealings lower as players took profits following record highs reached on Tuesday.
The DAX index of Germany's 30 leading shares ended down 13.55 points, or 0.5 percent, to 2,714.90, retreating from the record high of 2,728.64 reached briefly on Tuesday.
"We could be ready for a bit of a pause at the moment. But even if it goes down one percent, it's not really serious," one trader said.
Foreign exchange delers said dollar sentiment remained bullish and saw Wednesday's drift lower as consolidation rather than a change of track.
"It is really a matter of time before we get into really interesting territory and the dollar starts to square up for a test of 1.55 marks and 113 yen," said Bear Stearn's David Brown.
CURRENCIES AT 1620 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5373 marks and 112.15 yen, compared with 1.5394 marks and 112.29 yen in late European business on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS -- CLOSING INDICES
London - The FTSE index closed down 26.4 points, or 0.65 percent, at 4,024.4.
Frankfurt - The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt ended bourse trade down 13.55 at 2,714.90. In post-bourse computerised trade, the IBIS DAX ended down 13.67 at 2,705.06.
Paris - The CAC-40 share index closed down 9.76 points, or 0.45 percent, at 2,158.52. PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $381.75 gainst $381.45 on Tuesday. Silver ended three cents higher at $5.06.
